title: Deploy event points at the wrong change
source: Live calls to Token Factory (Nemotron-3.5 Lightning)

evidence.claim: Deploy increased retrieval top_k from 2 to 40 before incident, directly causing prompt expansion
Average input tokens jumped from 213 (baseline) to 3701 (incident), consistent with 20x more retrieved documents
At fixed high input tokens (1500-4000), varying concurrency from low (0-2) to high (10-inf) increases median latency from 0.48s to 1.07s (2.2x), showing concurrency amplifies latency
Same concurrency-stratified result confirms concurrency effect within incident window
Latency by concurrency in incident window shows low concurrency (0-2): 0.48s vs high concurrency (10-inf): 1.07s
No retries in either window (avg_retries=0, retry_breakdown shows 100% zero-retries), rejecting retry_storm

Cross-window comparison at low concurrency: baseline (input 0-500) 0.39s vs incident (input 1500-4000) 0.48s suggests prompt expansion adds ~0.09s baseline latency, but different app versions (v1 vs v4) limit certainty

rejected_hypotheses.why_rejected: Zero retries in both baseline and incident windows (call_1, call_5)
Deploy event (top_k 2→40) fully explains input token surge and subsequent latency/concurrency changes; no evidence of provider degradation independent of prompt size

uncertainties: Cannot isolate pure prompt-expansion effect at fixed concurrency within a single window (all incident requests have high input tokens); cross-window comparison confounded by app version change (v1→v4)
Concurrency increase (1→14.8) is likely a downstream consequence of slower per-request processing (Little's Law), not an independent root cause
recommended_actions: Roll back retrieval top_k from 40 to 2 (or a lower value) to reduce prompt size
Implement concurrency limiting / request queuing to prevent latency amplification under load
Add monitoring for input token distribution and per-request latency by prompt size

hypothesis_tests.hypothesis: High concurrency causes higher latency at fixed input token size
hypothesis_tests.result: At fixed input_tokens (1500-4000), median latency rises from 0.48s (concurrency 0-2, n=14) to 1.07s (concurrency 10-inf, n=160) — concurrency is a significant amplifier

hypothesis_tests.hypothesis: Large input tokens cause higher latency at fixed low concurrency
hypothesis_tests.result: Cross-window only: baseline (input 0-500, concurrency 0-2) 0.39s vs incident (input 1500-4000, concurrency 0-2) 0.48s. Suggests ~0.09s increase from prompt expansion, but confounded by app version change (v1→v4); within incident window all requests have high input tokens so cannot test directly
